Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) # Reoccurring *Salmonella* Cotham Outbreak Linked to Pet Bearded Dragons — United States, 2024 *Weekly* / August 21, 2025 / 74(31);474–479 Lingzi Xiaoli, PhD1; Paula Huth, MPH2; Cassandra Sherman, MPH3; Danielle Wroblewski, MS2; Stacy Anderson4; Lindsey Ferraro, MPH5; Dee Jones, DVM5; Molly Slaughter, MPH6; Brenda Morningstar, MS7; Tonya Mackie7; Natalee Bowen8; Molly Leeper, MPH1; Katie Werner, MPH1; Katharine Benedict, DVM, PhD1; Kate Varela, DVM1 ([View author affiliations](#contribAff)) ### **Summary** **What is already known about this topic?** Bearded dragons have been linked to *Salmonella* outbreaks, including a 2012–2014 *Salmonella* Cotham outbreak involving 160 patients in 35 states. **What is added by this report?** Twenty-seven cases (26 confirmed and one probable) of *S*. Cotham infection were identified during January 11–December 10, 2024. Eighteen reported cases were among persons with household exposure to bearded dragons; *S.* Cotham isolates from two bearded dragons kept in two patient households were closely genetically related to each other, to 2012–2014 isolates, and to clinical isolates from the 26 confirmed cases.
